q: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account (LMMH) of the Central and State Governments is issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
options.C: Controller General of Accounts
options.D: Railway Board

e: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account (LMMH) for the Central and State Governments is issued by the Controller General of Accounts in the Ministry of Finance.

q: Before the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is presented to Parliament, the budget proposals are approved by the:

options.A: Departmentally Related Standing Committee
options.B: Finance Commission
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Union Cabinet

e: Before the Budget is presented to Parliament, the budget proposals are approved by the Union Cabinet; standing committees, the Finance Commission and the CAG play no part in approving them.

q: The Budget document which explains, clause by clause, the provisions contained in the Finance Bill is the:

options.A: Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill
options.B: Budget at a Glance
options.C: Expenditure Profile
options.D: Detailed Demands for Grants

e: The Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill explains, clause by clause, the taxation provisions contained in the Finance Bill and is presented along with the Budget documents.

q: In the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, the estimates of revenue expenditure are presented Sub-Major Head-wise, while the estimates of capital expenditure are presented:

options.A: Minor Head-wise
options.B: Plan Head-wise
options.C: Primary Unit-wise
options.D: Suspense Head-wise

e: In the Railways' Demands for Grants, revenue expenditure estimates are presented Sub-Major Head-wise, while capital expenditure estimates are presented Plan Head-wise, following the plan classification of works.

q: The consolidated annual (Finance) accounts of the Indian Railways as a whole are compiled by the Railway Board on the basis of:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets received from stations
options.B: The Budget documents of the year
options.C: The Audit Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The monthly Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways, production units and other accounting units

e: The Railway Board compiles the consolidated annual Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways from the monthly Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways, production units and other accounting units.

q: Which of the following receipts is NOT classified under 'Other Coaching Earnings' of the Railways?

options.A: Receipts from parcels and luggage traffic
options.B: Receipts from the carriage of postal mails
options.C: Receipts from platform tickets and retiring rooms
options.D: Freight receipts from goods traffic

e: Freight receipts from goods traffic are Goods earnings, not Other Coaching Earnings; parcels and luggage, postal mails, platform tickets and retiring rooms are the coaching-side receipts.

q: Which of the following is NOT a 'Sundry Other Earning' of the Railways?

options.A: Wharfage charges
options.B: Earnings from advertisements displayed at stations
options.C: Rent and licence fee of railway land and buildings
options.D: Earnings from leasing of railway premises

e: Wharfage is a charge on goods traffic for goods kept at stations beyond the free time and is a Goods earning; advertisements, rent and licence fee of land and buildings and leasing of premises are Sundry Other Earnings.

q: The 'Effective Revenue Deficit' of the Government represents the revenue deficit excluding:

options.A: Interest payments
options.B: Grants-in-aid given for the creation of capital assets
options.C: Expenditure on subsidies
options.D: Capital expenditure

e: Effective Revenue Deficit is the revenue deficit excluding grants-in-aid given for the creation of capital assets, since that part of the revenue spending actually results in assets.

q: The annual Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes of the Railways, presented in connection with the Budget, collectively comprise the Works Programme (Pink Book), the Rolling Stock Programme and the:

options.A: Earnings Programme
options.B: Traffic Programme
options.C: Machinery and Plant Programme
options.D: Stores Programme

e: The three annual programmes presented with the Budget are the Works Programme (Pink Book), the Rolling Stock Programme and the Machinery and Plant Programme.

q: The General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, which lay down the general financial principles applicable to Government departments, are issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Controller General of Accounts
options.C: NITI Aayog
options.D: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance

e: The General Financial Rules, 2017 are issued by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, and lay down the general financial principles to be followed by Government departments.

q: The Finance Accounts of the Railways differ from the Appropriation Accounts in that the Finance Accounts:

options.A: Present the receipts and disbursements of the year classified under the Major Heads of account
options.B: Compare the expenditure of the year with the grants voted by Parliament
options.C: Are prepared only for the transactions of the Railway Board's office
options.D: Contain the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General

e: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the year classified under the Major Heads of account; comparing expenditure with the grants voted by Parliament is the function of the Appropriation Accounts.

q: The balances outstanding under the suspense and remittance heads at the close of a financial year:

options.A: Lapse to the Government at the close of the year
options.B: Are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance
options.C: Are written off automatically
options.D: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund

e: Balances outstanding under the suspense and remittance heads do not lapse at the close of the financial year; they are carried forward to the next year and cleared as the underlying transactions are settled.

q: Which of the following railway units is an independent accounting unit rendering its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board?

options.A: A railway division
options.B: A production unit, such as the Integral Coach Factory
options.C: A large railway station
options.D: A sub-divisional engineering office

e: A production unit such as the Integral Coach Factory is an independent accounting unit and renders its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board; divisions and stations account through their zonal railway.

q: Treasury Bills, through which the Government of India raises short-term funds, are issued on its behalf by the:

options.A: State Bank of India
options.B: Ministry of Finance directly
options.C: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.D: Reserve Bank of India

e: Treasury Bills, the instrument for the Government of India's short-term borrowing, are issued on behalf of the Government by the Reserve Bank of India.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Internal Debt of the Central Government is classified under Major Head:
e: The Internal Debt of the Central Government is classified under Major Head 6001; Major Head 6002 covers External Debt and 4000 is Capital Outlay on non-specific heads.

q: Which of the following items of expenditure is 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Debt charges, including interest and repayment of public debt
options.C: Cost of construction of new lines
options.D: Salaries of the staff of the Railway Board

e: Debt charges, including interest on and repayment of public debt, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted; the DRF appropriation, new line construction and Railway Board staff salaries are voted items.

q: Besides recommending the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy also recommended the setting up of an independent regulator for the Railways, namely the:

options.A: Railway Claims Tribunal
options.B: Rail Land Development Authority
options.C: Rail Development Authority
options.D: Railway Recruitment Board

e: The committee chaired by Bibek Debroy recommended, besides merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the setting up of the Rail Development Authority as an independent regulator for the Railways.

q: An 'Excess Grant' differs from a 'Supplementary Grant' in that an Excess Grant is:

options.A: Obtained before the expenditure is incurred
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Not required to be covered by an Appropriation Act
options.D: Obtained after the close of the financial year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the sanctioned grant

e: An Excess Grant is obtained after the close of the financial year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the sanctioned grant; a Supplementary Grant, by contrast, is obtained during the year before the excess occurs.

q: Where expenditure on a 'new service' can be financed by re-appropriation of savings within the grant, but the approval of Parliament is nevertheless required, that approval is obtained by presenting:

options.A: A token supplementary demand for a nominal amount
options.B: An Excess Grant
options.C: A Vote of Credit
options.D: An Exceptional Grant

e: Where savings within the grant can finance a new service but Parliament's approval is still required, that approval is obtained through a token supplementary demand of a nominal amount, the money coming from the re-appropriation.

q: An imprest (permanent advance) held by an officer is recouped, that is, restored to its sanctioned amount, when the holder:

options.A: Submits his monthly salary bill
options.B: Renders the paid vouchers for the amounts spent out of the imprest
options.C: Completes one year in the post
options.D: Obtains a fresh sanction every month

e: An imprest is recouped, that is restored to its sanctioned amount, when the holder renders the paid vouchers for the sums spent out of it; the Accounts Office replenishes only the amount actually vouched.

q: The Preliminary Works Programme (PWP) of a zonal railway differs from the Final Works Programme (FWP) in that the PWP contains:

options.A: Only works which have already been sanctioned
options.B: The audited figures of works expenditure
options.C: The proposals submitted by the zonal railway, while the FWP contains the works finally approved by the Railway Board
options.D: Only works relating to safety

e: The Preliminary Works Programme contains the works proposals submitted by the zonal railway, while the Final Works Programme contains the works finally approved by the Railway Board after scrutiny of those proposals.

q: In the system of apportionment of earnings, the earnings from through traffic are initially brought to account in full by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The railway at which the traffic terminates
options.C: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The railway on which the traffic originates, that is, the collecting railway, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned

e: Earnings from through traffic are first brought to account in full by the railway on which the traffic originates, the collecting railway, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned through apportionment.

q: The Budget documents presented to Parliament disclose the estimated receipts and disbursements of the Government under all the three parts of Government accounts, namely:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund, the Contingency Fund and the Public Account
options.B: The Consolidated Fund only
options.C: The Public Account only
options.D: The Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund only

e: The Budget documents presented to Parliament disclose the estimated receipts and disbursements under all three parts of Government accounts - the Consolidated Fund, the Contingency Fund and the Public Account.

q: The monthly Account Current of a zonal railway is rendered to the Railway Board by the:

options.A: General Manager
options.B: Principal Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.C: Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Chief Commercial Manager

e: The monthly Account Current of a zonal railway is rendered to the Railway Board by the Principal Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer, who heads the railway's accounts organisation.

q: Materials released from a capital work and returned to the stores stock are accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Crediting the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Crediting the cost of the work concerned, thereby reducing the capital cost of the work
options.D: Treating the value as a fresh purchase of stores

e: Materials released from a capital work and returned to stores stock are credited to the cost of the work concerned, so that the capital cost of the work is reduced by the value recovered.

q: For the purposes of the Appropriation Accounts and the regularisation of excess expenditure, the excess or saving under a Demand is reckoned with reference to:

options.A: Each Primary Unit separately
options.B: Each Sub-Major Head separately
options.C: Each individual work separately
options.D: The total amount of the Grant (Demand) as a whole

e: For the Appropriation Accounts and regularisation of excesses, the excess or saving is reckoned with reference to the total amount of the Grant (Demand) as a whole, not against each sub-head or work separately.

q: The Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme of the Railways deals with:

options.A: Procurement and replacement of machinery and plant required for workshops and the open line
options.B: Manufacture of locomotives and coaches
options.C: Purchase of stores for stocking in depots
options.D: Construction of staff quarters

e: The Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme deals with the procurement and replacement of machinery and plant required for workshops and the open line; locomotives and coaches fall under the Rolling Stock Programme.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume I, deals with the compilation of the general accounts of a railway.
2. The Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume II, deals with Traffic Accounts, including station accounts and the Traffic Book.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume I deals with the compilation of the general accounts of a railway, and Volume II deals with Traffic Accounts, including station accounts and the Traffic Book.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balances of the State Railway Provident Fund form part of the Public Account of India.
2. Disbursements out of the Public Account require an appropriation by Parliament in the same manner as withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the balances of the State Railway Provident Fund form part of the Public Account of India. Statement 2 is wrong - disbursements from the Public Account, being trustee moneys, do not require appropriation by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed by Parliament.
2. The Demands for Grants presented to the Lok Sabha cover both voted expenditure and expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed. Statement 2 is wrong - the Demands for Grants submitted for voting cover only voted expenditure; charged expenditure is shown separately.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A 'New Service' means expenditure on a new activity or service arising out of a fresh policy decision, which was not contemplated in the approved Budget.
2. A 'New Instrument of Service' means expenditure incurred through a new instrument or agency for rendering a service which already exists.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a New Service is expenditure on a new activity arising from a fresh policy decision, while a New Instrument of Service is expenditure through a new instrument or agency for rendering a service that already exists.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are classified as revenue expenditure under Major Head 3002.
2. Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are operated as a suspense head, pending recovery or adjustment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 2 is correct: Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are operated as a suspense head pending recovery or adjustment. Statement 1 is wrong - Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are not classified as revenue expenditure under Major Head 3002.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The appropriation made from revenue to the Railway Pension Fund is classified under Sub-Major Head 12, 'Appropriations to Funds'.
2. The pensionary charges actually paid to retired railway servants are classified under Sub-Major Head 13.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the appropriation from revenue to the Railway Pension Fund is classified under Sub-Major Head 12, Appropriations to Funds, while the pensionary charges actually paid out are classified under Sub-Major Head 13.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transfer transactions between two zonal railways are adjusted through the books of the Railway Board under the head 'Transfer Railways'.
2. Transfer transactions between two accounting units of the same zonal railway are adjusted within the books of that railway itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: transfer transactions between two zonal railways are adjusted through the books of the Railway Board under the head Transfer Railways, while transfers between units of the same railway are adjusted within that railway's own books.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An excess of expenditure over the allotment under a sub-head, where the total amount of the Grant is not exceeded, can be regularised by re-appropriation.
2. An excess of expenditure over the total amount of a Grant can likewise be regularised by re-appropriation, provided savings are available under another Grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: an excess under a sub-head can be regularised by re-appropriation so long as the total Grant is not exceeded. Statement 2 is wrong - an excess over the Grant itself cannot be cured by re-appropriation from another Grant.

q: Part B of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of:

options.A: Coaching earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry other earnings
options.D: Military traffic earnings

e: Part B of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of goods earnings among the railways concerned; coaching earnings apportionment is dealt with in a separate part of the Traffic Book.

q: Items under the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' are cleared from the head when:

options.A: The cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: The bill is passed for payment
options.C: The cheque is presented by the payee at his bank
options.D: The bank's intimation or advice of payment of the cheque is received

e: Items under Cheques and Bills are cleared from the suspense head when the bank's intimation or advice of payment of the cheque is received, confirming that the payee has actually been paid.

q: Balances under the suspense head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' are cleared:

options.A: On receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: Automatically at the end of five years
options.C: By write-off with the sanction of the General Manager
options.D: Only after the statutory audit is completed

e: Balances under Reserve Bank Suspense are cleared on receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India confirming the transaction, and not by write-off or lapse of time.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transfer transactions originating in the books of a unit are 'outward transfers' for that unit.
2. The same transactions are 'inward transfers' for the respondent unit which receives the advice.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: transfer transactions originating in a unit's books are outward transfers for that unit, and the very same transactions are inward transfers for the respondent unit that receives the advice.

q: The Consolidated Fund of India and the Public Account of India are constituted under Article ___ of the Constitution:
e: Article 266 of the Constitution constitutes the Consolidated Fund of India and the Public Account of India; Article 267 relates to the Contingency Fund and Article 265 prohibits levy of tax except by authority of law.

q: The constitutional provision that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law is contained in Article:
e: Article 265 lays down that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law, so every tax must be backed by a valid law enacted by the competent legislature.

q: If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of which of the following is final?

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Union Finance Minister
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final under the Constitution.

q: The expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including the salaries and allowances of its Chairman and members, are:

options.A: Voted by Parliament every year
options.B: Charged on the Public Account of India
options.C: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Borne jointly by the Union and the States

e: The expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including the salaries and allowances of its Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted annually.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salaries and allowances of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.
2. The pensions of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the salaries and allowances of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned, while their pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: A temporary imprest differs from a permanent (standing) imprest in that a temporary imprest:

options.A: Is always of a larger amount
options.B: Is granted for a specific purpose or occasion and must be accounted for as soon as that purpose is over
options.C: Does not require any vouchers in support of the expenditure
options.D: Can be held only by a gazetted officer

e: A temporary imprest is granted for a specific purpose or occasion and must be accounted for as soon as that purpose is over; a permanent imprest, by contrast, continues with the holder and is recouped from time to time.

q: Sub-vouchers in support of small contingent payments made by a disbursing officer are ordinarily:

options.A: Retained by the disbursing officer in his office and not forwarded to the Accounts Office
options.B: Destroyed immediately after the payment is made
options.C: Sent directly to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Published along with the monthly accounts of the railway

e: Sub-vouchers supporting small contingent payments are ordinarily retained by the disbursing officer in his own office and are not forwarded to the Accounts Office, which receives the consolidated bill.

q: The Capital Fund of the Railways is credited with:

options.A: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.B: A share of the cess levied on petrol and diesel
options.C: Dividends received from railway public sector undertakings
options.D: Appropriations made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways

e: The Capital Fund is credited with appropriations made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways, and the fund so built up finances capital works from the Railways' internal resources.

q: A work of passenger amenities financed from the Development Fund is classified under the allocation:

options.A: Capital-5300

e: A passenger amenities work bears Plan Head 53; when it is financed from the Development Fund, the allocation combines the fund and the Plan Head as DF-5300.

q: In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, the Capital-at-charge is shown on:

options.A: The liabilities side
options.B: The assets side
options.C: Both the liabilities and the assets sides
options.D: Neither side, as it appears only in the Block Account

e: Capital-at-charge is shown on the liabilities side of the railway Balance Sheet, since it represents the capital provided to the Railways, against which the block assets appear on the assets side.

q: In the Indian Railway Finance Code, the provisions relating to 'New Service' and 'New Instrument of Service' are contained in para:
e: The provisions relating to New Service and New Instrument of Service are contained in para 370 of the Indian Railway Finance Code.

q: The National Investment Fund (NIF) of the Government of India is credited mainly with:

options.A: The proceeds of spectrum auctions
options.B: The compensation cess collected under the GST
options.C: The net proceeds of the taxes shared with the States
options.D: The proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises

e: The National Investment Fund was created to hold the proceeds realised from disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises, the income being used mainly for social sector schemes and revival of viable PSUs.

q: The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) is financed mainly by:

options.A: Toll collections on national highways
options.B: A cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel
options.C: Market borrowings raised by the National Highways Authority of India
options.D: The safety surcharge levied on railway passenger fares

e: The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is fed by a cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel, and the proceeds are used for development of road and other infrastructure.

q: 'Effective Capital Expenditure' of the Government, as shown in the Budget documents, represents:

options.A: Capital expenditure together with grants-in-aid given for the creation of capital assets
options.B: Capital expenditure minus depreciation of assets
options.C: Revenue expenditure and capital expenditure taken together
options.D: The fiscal deficit minus the interest payments of the year

e: Effective Capital Expenditure means the capital expenditure of the Government together with grants-in-aid given to States and others specifically for the creation of capital assets.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is:

options.A: A company owned jointly by the Railways and private investors
options.B: A joint venture of the Ministry of Railways and the State Governments
options.C: A wholly Government-owned company under the Ministry of Railways
options.D: A statutory corporation set up by the Reserve Bank of India

e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation is a wholly Government-owned company under the administrative control of the Ministry of Railways, raising market borrowings for financing rolling stock and projects.

q: The arithmetical accuracy of the monthly accounts compiled in the General Books is proved by preparing a:

options.A: Classified Abstract
options.B: Debt Head Report
options.C: Suspense Register
options.D: Trial Balance

e: The arithmetical accuracy of the monthly accounts compiled in the General Books is proved by the Trial Balance, which tests that total debits equal total credits.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the interest payments of the Central Government are classified under Major Head:
e: In the list of Major and Minor Heads, interest payments of the Central Government are classified under Major Head 2049 - Interest Payments, covering interest on internal and external debt.

q: Works costing less than the prescribed limit, which are not shown individually in the Pink Book, are provided for in the Works Programme:

options.A: In bulk, as lump sum provisions
options.B: Under the head 'Other Specified Works' only
options.C: In the Rolling Stock Programme
options.D: Only after a supplementary grant is obtained

e: Small works costing less than the prescribed limit, which are not listed individually in the Pink Book, are provided for in bulk as lump sum provisions in the Works Programme.

q: Under exchequer control, the expenditure of the Ministries and Departments during the year is regulated through:

options.A: Budget proportions fixed by the Railway Board
options.B: Monthly statements of re-appropriation
options.C: Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year

e: Under exchequer control, expenditure of Ministries is regulated against Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans so that spending stays within the authorised cash flow.

q: Treasury Bills issued by the Government of India are:

options.A: Long-term dated securities carrying a printed coupon rate
options.B: Securities issued only to the State Governments
options.C: A part of the Public Account of India
options.D: Zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value

e: Treasury Bills are short-term zero-coupon instruments of the Government of India, issued at a discount to face value and redeemed at par on maturity.

q: The principal accounting adviser to the Government of India in matters of accounting is the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Controller General of Accounts
options.C: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Finance Secretary to the Government of India

e: The Controller General of Accounts, in the Ministry of Finance, is the principal accounting adviser to the Government of India on accounting matters and compiles the Union Government accounts.

q: The separation of accounts from audit in the Union Government, that is, the departmentalisation of accounts, was introduced in the year:
e: Departmentalisation of Union Government accounts, separating accounts from audit and making departments responsible for their own accounts, was introduced in 1976.

q: The Railways maintain certain lines for strategic (defence) considerations. The working losses of such Strategic Lines are:

options.A: Borne by the Development Fund
options.B: Borne by the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Borne by General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways on strategic considerations
options.D: Written off against the Capital Fund

e: Working losses of Strategic Lines, maintained for defence considerations, are reimbursed to the Railways by General Revenues, so the burden does not fall on railway finances.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the Contingency Fund of India forms:

options.A: Part I of the Government accounts
options.B: Part III of the Government accounts
options.C: A section of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Part II of the Government accounts

e: In the Government accounts, Part I is the Consolidated Fund, Part II is the Contingency Fund of India, and Part III is the Public Account.

q: The Railway Convention Committee, which reviews the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances, is ordinarily constituted:

options.A: Every year, along with the Budget
options.B: Once in five years
options.C: Once in ten years
options.D: Only once, at the time of separation of railway finances

e: The Railway Convention Committee, which reviews the rate of dividend and the financial relationship between Railways and General Finances, is ordinarily constituted once in five years.

q: The market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation:

options.A: Do not form part of the internal debt of the Government of India and are serviced by the Railways through lease charges
options.B: Form part of the internal debt of the Government of India
options.C: Are serviced directly out of the Consolidated Fund of India as charged expenditure
options.D: Are guaranteed to be repaid out of the Contingency Fund of India

e: IRFC borrowings are not part of the internal debt of the Government of India; the Railways service them through lease charges paid to IRFC.

q: Which of the following forms a component of 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway accounts?

options.A: Security deposits received from contractors
options.B: The accumulated balances of the Railway Funds
options.C: Station earnings remitted but not yet credited by the bank
options.D: Wages remaining unpaid at the end of the month

e: Cash-in-Transit covers remittances in the course of collection, such as station earnings remitted by a station but not yet credited by the bank to the Railways' account.

q: The construction of staff quarters, when financed from the Development Fund as a labour welfare work, is classified under the allocation:

options.A: Capital-5100

e: Staff quarters financed from the Development Fund as a labour welfare work are classified under the allocation DF-5100, combining the Development Fund source with Plan Head 5100 for staff quarters.

q: Which of the following works is NOT normally financed from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: Passenger amenity works at stations
options.B: Construction of a new railway line
options.C: Labour welfare works
options.D: Unremunerative operational improvement works

e: Construction of a new railway line is a capital work charged to Capital (Major Head 5002); the Development Fund finances amenities, welfare and unremunerative improvement works, not new lines.

q: Supplementary Demands for Grants are:

options.A: Voted by the Lok Sabha following the same procedure as the main Demands for Grants
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Approved by the Finance Minister without any vote of Parliament
options.D: Incorporated in the Appropriation Act automatically, without discussion

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are presented to and voted by the Lok Sabha following the same procedure as the main Demands for Grants.

q: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) paid to a retired railway servant covered under the old pension scheme is debited to:

options.A: The working expenses under Major Head 3002
options.B: The Development Fund
options.C: The Railway Pension Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Pensionary charges of railway servants under the old pension scheme, including DCRG, are met from the Railway Pension Fund, which is fed by appropriations from revenue.

q: The General Books of a zonal railway are closed and balanced:

options.A: Every day
options.B: Every week
options.C: Once in a year
options.D: Every month

e: The General Books of a zonal railway are closed and balanced every month, forming the basis of the monthly Account Current rendered to the Railway Board.

q: The accounts of a division of a zonal railway are:

options.A: Rendered directly to the Railway Board in the form of a monthly Account Current
options.B: Incorporated into the accounts of the zonal railway, which renders the Account Current to the Railway Board
options.C: Compiled by the Controller General of Accounts
options.D: Maintained wholly outside the railway accounts

e: Divisional accounts are incorporated into the accounts of the zonal railway, and it is the zonal railway that renders the monthly Account Current to the Railway Board.

q: The consolidated Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways, before being laid before Parliament, are:

options.A: Audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Approved by the Railway Convention Committee
options.C: Certified by the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Passed by a vote of the Lok Sabha

e: The consolidated Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India before being laid before Parliament.

q: The custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, and the payments into and withdrawals from them, are regulated by law made by Parliament under Article:
e: Article 283 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate by law the custody of the Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund and payments into and withdrawals from them.

q: The distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States is recommended by the body constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution, namely the:

options.A: NITI Aayog
options.B: Goods and Services Tax Council
options.C: Estimates Committee of Parliament
options.D: Finance Commission

e: The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280, recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States and the shares of the States.

q: The administrative expenses of the Supreme Court of India, including the salaries and allowances of its officers and servants, are:

options.A: Voted by Parliament every year
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Borne by the State Governments
options.D: Met out of the Public Account of India

e: The administrative expenses of the Supreme Court, including salaries and allowances of its officers and servants, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted.

q: The President of India cannot return which of the following for the reconsideration of Parliament?

options.A: A Money Bill
options.B: An ordinary Bill passed by both Houses
options.C: A Private Member's Bill passed by both Houses
options.D: A State Bill reserved for the consideration of the President

e: The President may return a Bill for reconsideration, but a Money Bill cannot be returned; the President must either assent to it or withhold assent.

q: In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, explanations for the variations between the Final Grant and the actual expenditure are required to be furnished:

options.A: For every variation, however small
options.B: Only for variations in charged expenditure
options.C: For variations which exceed the prescribed limits
options.D: Only when the total grant as a whole is exceeded

e: In the Appropriation Accounts, explanations for variations between Final Grant and actual expenditure are required only for variations exceeding the prescribed monetary or percentage limits.

q: When the holder of an imprest is transferred from his post, he is required to:

options.A: Retain the imprest amount until his successor demands it
options.B: Deposit the imprest balance in the Public Account in his own name
options.C: Spend the unspent balance before handing over charge
options.D: Account for the imprest in full and hand over the balance to his successor

e: On transfer, the holder of an imprest must account for it in full and hand over the unspent balance to his successor, who gives a receipt for it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under the head 'Transfer Railways' remain outstanding because cash is physically transferred from one railway to another.
2. Balances under the head 'Transfer Railways' represent inter-railway transfer transactions awaiting final adjustment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: no cash physically moves between railways. Statement 2 is true: Transfer Railways balances represent inter-railway transfer transactions awaiting final adjustment. Hence 2 only.

q: A change in the allocation (classification) of an item of expenditure, decided during the course of a financial year, is given effect to in the accounts from:

options.A: The date of the decision, with retrospective effect from the beginning of that year
options.B: The commencement of the next financial year
options.C: The accounts of the next month following the decision
options.D: The March (Final) accounts of the same year

e: A change in the allocation of expenditure decided during a year takes effect from the commencement of the next financial year, so that the accounts of a year follow one uniform classification.

q: An item of expenditure is booked in the accounts under the head prescribed by the classification of accounts, even though budget provision for it happens to exist under a different head. This is because:

options.A: Correct classification is followed irrespective of the head under which budget provision exists
options.B: Budget provision automatically alters the classification of the item
options.C: The classification of an item is decided by the spending unit itself
options.D: The Accounts Office may ignore classification wherever budget provision exists

e: Classification of an item follows the prescribed head of account on the basis of its nature; the existence of budget provision under another head does not alter its correct classification.

q: The erstwhile Demand No. 1 (Railway Board) and Demand No. 2 (Miscellaneous Expenditure) of the separate Railway Budget are now accounted for under Major Head:
e: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the erstwhile Demand No. 1 (Railway Board) and Demand No. 2 (Miscellaneous Expenditure) are accounted under Major Head 3001.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Plan Heads are used for the classification of works (capital) expenditure included in the Works Programme.
2. Revenue working expenses are classified through Sub-Major Heads and Primary Units, and not through Plan Heads.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: Plan Heads classify works (capital) expenditure in the Works Programme, while revenue working expenses are classified through Sub-Major Heads and Primary Units, not Plan Heads.

q: An existing asset is renewed by a materially better and heavier asset. The cost of the renewal is apportioned as under:

options.A: The entire cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The entire cost is charged to Capital
options.C: The entire cost is shared equally between the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Capital
options.D: The cost of the like-for-like (original) element is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the additional cost of betterment to Capital/Development Fund

e: On renewal with a better and heavier asset, the like-for-like cost of the original asset is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the extra cost of betterment to Capital or Development Fund.

q: The net earnings, if any, of a new railway line under construction, before it is opened for public traffic, are:

options.A: Credited to the revenue earnings of the year
options.B: Credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of its cost
options.C: Credited to the Development Fund
options.D: Treated as Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways

e: Net earnings of a new line during construction, before it opens for public traffic, are credited to the Capital account of the work, reducing its cost.

q: The Traffic Book of a zonal railway is compiled in:

options.A: The Traffic Accounts Office, from the station balance sheets and the apportionment statements
options.B: The Cash & Pay Office of the zonal railway
options.C: The Railway Board's office, directly from the returns rendered by stations
options.D: The Divisional Accounts Office

e: The Traffic Book is compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office from the station balance sheets and the apportionment statements of earnings.

q: Earnings arising from 'local traffic' — traffic which both originates and terminates on the same railway — are:

options.A: Apportioned among all the zonal railways
options.B: Credited entirely to the Railway Board
options.C: Shared equally with the railway serving the destination station
options.D: Retained wholly by that railway and are not subject to apportionment

e: Earnings from local traffic, which both originates and terminates on the same railway, are retained wholly by that railway and are not apportioned.

q: Apportionment of earnings among the zonal railways becomes necessary mainly because:

options.A: Through traffic travels over two or more railways, while the fare/freight for the whole journey is collected by a single railway
options.B: Each zonal railway maintains a separate cash balance with the Reserve Bank
options.C: Stations render their balance sheets to different accounts offices
options.D: The Railway Board requires it purely for statistical purposes

e: Through traffic travels over two or more railways but the fare or freight for the whole journey is collected by one railway, so the earnings must be apportioned among the railways concerned.

q: The suspense head 'PSB Suspense' in railway accounts is operated for transactions relating to:

options.A: Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries/Departments
options.B: Public sector banks, pending receipt of advices and settlement
options.C: The Reserve Bank of India, Central Accounts Section
options.D: State Governments and their Accountants General

e: PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with public sector banks, such as remittances and collections, pending receipt of bank advices and final settlement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Suspense heads are final heads of account in the railway classification of accounts.
2. Balances under suspense heads represent amounts recoverable or payable, pending clearance to the final heads of account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: suspense heads are temporary, not final heads. Statement 2 is true: their balances represent amounts recoverable or payable pending clearance to the final heads. Hence 2 only.

q: The Government Accounting Rules, 1990, which lay down the rules relating to the forms and compilation of Government accounts, were issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Railway Board
options.C: Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance

e: The Government Accounting Rules, 1990, governing the forms and compilation of Government accounts, were issued by the Controller General of Accounts in the Ministry of Finance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund form part of the working expenses of the Railways.
2. Such appropriations are charged to revenue under Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Pension Fund form part of working expenses, booked under Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Refunds of fares and freight granted to the public are treated as a reduction of the earnings of the Railways.
2. Recoveries of amounts overpaid to staff or contractors are treated as a reduction of expenditure under the head originally debited.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: refunds of fares and freight are treated as a reduction of earnings, and recoveries of overpayments are treated as a reduction of expenditure under the head originally debited.

q: The 'door-step banking' arrangement for the collection of station earnings was introduced mainly to:

options.A: Increase the cash balance retained at stations
options.B: Reduce 'Cash-in-Transit' and ensure prompt credit of earnings to the Railways' account
options.C: Dispense with the rendering of station balance sheets
options.D: Enable payment of salaries to station staff in cash

e: Door-step banking arranges collection of station earnings at the station itself, reducing Cash-in-Transit and ensuring prompt credit of the earnings to the Railways' account.

q: The Budget Estimates of a zonal railway, before submission to the Railway Board, are finally approved at the zonal level by the:

options.A: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: Chief Operations Manager
options.C: Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: General Manager

e: The Budget Estimates of a zonal railway are finally approved at the zonal level by the General Manager before submission to the Railway Board.

q: The distribution of a voted grant among the various spending units and offices, for incurring expenditure, is known as:

options.A: Budget Allotment
options.B: Appropriation
options.C: Re-appropriation
options.D: Surrender of funds

e: Budget Allotment is the distribution of a voted grant among the various spending units and offices authorised to incur expenditure against it.

q: Savings available under one Demand for Grant:

options.A: Can be freely utilised to meet excess expenditure under another Demand
options.B: Are transferred to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Cannot be used to meet excess expenditure under another Demand; the excess requires regularisation by an Excess Grant for that Demand itself
options.D: Lapse automatically to the Railway Funds

e: Each Demand for Grant is voted separately, so savings under one Demand cannot meet excess under another; the excess must be regularised by an Excess Grant for that Demand itself.

q: Before a Demand for Excess Grant is presented to the Lok Sabha, the excess expenditure is first examined by the:

options.A: Estimates Committee
options.B: Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Railway Convention Committee
options.D: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: Before a Demand for Excess Grant is presented, the excess expenditure is examined by the Public Accounts Committee, which reports on its regularisation.

q: Expenditure 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India is:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of both Houses of Parliament
options.B: Submitted to the vote of the Rajya Sabha only
options.C: Neither discussed nor voted upon in Parliament
options.D: Not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed

e: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, although it may be discussed in the House.
